category_a.name: Context_Window_Overflow
category_a.definition: Agent cannot process all provided input because cumulative context exceeds capacity, leading to information loss within a single processing step.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent drops or cannot access portions of the input due to exceeding context window limits in a single interaction.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When information loss occurs between multi-hop iterations (use A.12). When output is truncated but input was fully processed (use A.3).
detection_heuristics: Error messages referencing context length or token limits
Agent acknowledges it cannot see all provided information
Missing references to content that was included in the prompt
Explicit truncation warnings in logs or output
Input token count exceeds model's documented context window

category_a.name: External_Retrieval_System_Failure
category_a.definition: External retrieval system fails to return passages, returns error, or produces unusable results, blocking pipeline progression.
category_a.when_to_use: When the external retrieval component fails to provide required information, returns errors, or produces malformed results.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When retrieval succeeds but returns irrelevant content (content quality issue, not architecture failure). When agent fails to use retrieved content properly (use A.12 or B-codes).
detection_heuristics: HTTP errors or API failures from retrieval endpoint
Empty retrieval results when documents exist
Malformed or unparseable retrieval responses
Retrieval timeout or connection errors
Agent explicitly states retrieval failed or returned no results

category_a.name: Output_Truncation_Or_Absence
category_a.definition: Agent produces no output, empty output, or incomplete output that cuts off mid-sentence or mid-field without proper termination, indicating generation failure.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent fails to produce complete, substantive output - either generating nothing, only whitespace, or stopping prematurely during generation.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When output is complete but incorrect in content (use B-codes). When truncation is due to explicit user interruption. When output is intentionally brief but complete.
detection_heuristics: Output ends mid-sentence without punctuation or closing markers
Required output fields are empty, null, or contain only whitespace
JSON/XML structures are incomplete or unclosed
Output length is suspiciously short relative to task complexity
No substantive content generated despite task requirements
Generation stops without completion markers or acknowledgment

category_a.name: Task_Execution_Timeout
category_a.definition: Agent execution exceeds allocated time budget and is forcibly terminated before completing its task.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent's processing is stopped due to time constraints, regardless of output quality.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When output is truncated but no timeout occurred (use A.3). When the agent completes quickly but with poor quality (use B-codes).
detection_heuristics: System timeout errors in logs
Execution time exceeds configured threshold
Forced termination signals in system monitoring
Incomplete processing with timestamp evidence of cutoff
Timeout exception traces in error logs

category_a.name: Memory_Exhaustion
category_a.definition: Agent exceeds available memory allocation during execution, causing failure or degraded performance.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent runs out of memory resources during processing, leading to crashes or severe performance degradation.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When memory is sufficient but context window is exceeded (use A.1). When performance issues are not memory-related.
detection_heuristics: Out-of-memory errors in logs
Memory usage metrics exceed thresholds
Process killed by OS/container due to memory limits
Severe performance degradation correlated with memory pressure
Swap/paging activity indicating memory exhaustion

category_a.name: Repetitive_Output_Looping
category_a.definition: Agent generates repetitive or cyclical content, producing the same or highly similar output multiple times without making progress toward task completion.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent gets stuck in a loop, repeating phrases, sentences, or reasoning patterns without advancing toward the goal.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When repetition is intentional (e.g., emphasizing a point). When agent makes incremental progress despite some repeated elements.
detection_heuristics: Identical or near-identical phrases repeated multiple times consecutively
Same reasoning steps repeated without new information
Output contains obvious copy-paste patterns
Length increases without informational progress
High n-gram overlap within same output

category_a.name: Task_Refusal_Or_Abandonment
category_a.definition: Agent explicitly refuses to perform the assigned task, states it cannot complete the work, or abandons the task mid-execution without valid justification.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent actively declines to perform the task or gives up, regardless of whether the task is within its capabilities.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When the agent attempts the task but produces incorrect results (use B-codes). When refusal is appropriate (e.g., unsafe requests).
detection_heuristics: Explicit statements like 'I cannot do this' or 'I'm unable to complete this task'
Agent requests clarification instead of attempting the task
Agent switches to explaining why task is difficult rather than attempting it
Partial attempt followed by explicit abandonment statement
Agent suggests alternative tasks instead of attempting the assigned one

category_a.name: Execution_Error_Or_Exception
category_a.definition: System-level runtime error or exception occurs during agent execution, causing failure or abnormal termination.
category_a.when_to_use: When technical errors (parsing failures, API errors, code exceptions) prevent normal agent operation.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When the agent completes execution but with poor output quality (use B-codes). When error is specifically retrieval-related (use A.2).
detection_heuristics: Stack traces or exception messages in logs
HTTP 5xx errors from agent endpoints
Parsing errors for structured input/output
Runtime exceptions in execution logs
System error codes indicating abnormal termination

category_a.name: Instruction_Compliance_Failure
category_a.definition: Agent ignores or violates explicit instructions from system prompts, user requests, or output format specifications, producing responses that fail to follow the given directives.
category_a.when_to_use: When the agent demonstrably ignores clear instructions, answers the wrong question, violates format requirements, or disregards constraints specified in the prompt.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When the agent attempts to follow instructions but makes content errors (use B-codes). When instructions are ambiguous or contradictory. When output is incomplete due to truncation (use A.3).
detection_heuristics: Required output format (JSON, XML, etc.) is not followed
Agent addresses a different question than asked
Explicit constraints (length, style, structure) are violated
System prompt instructions are ignored (e.g., role-playing directives)
Agent produces disallowed content types despite restrictions
Required fields or sections are missing from structured output
Agent performs operations explicitly forbidden in instructions

category_a.name: Inter_Hop_Information_Loss
category_a.definition: Critical information from previous retrieval iterations is lost or not carried forward to subsequent hops, breaking the chain of reasoning in multi-hop retrieval scenarios.
category_a.when_to_use: When information successfully processed in earlier retrieval iterations is unavailable or ignored in later iterations, specific to multi-hop architectures.
category_a.when_not_to_use: When initial context cannot fit in a single interaction (use A.1). When agent fails to use available context properly (use B-codes). When the pipeline is not multi-hop.
detection_heuristics: Agent re-asks questions answered in previous hops
Facts established in hop N are contradicted or ignored in hop N+1
Agent states it lacks information that was retrieved earlier
Reasoning chains break between iterations without context overflow
State management logs show information not passed between hops
Agent treats later hops as independent rather than building on prior work

category_b.name: Solver_Inadequate_Retrieval_Guidance
category_b.definition: Solver fails to produce summary with sufficient specificity for the retrieval system to fetch relevant documents. This includes failing to identify and explicitly name all entities requiring verification, using vague or ambiguous descriptions, providing incomplete entity information, or omitting critical search terms.
category_b.when_to_use: When solver's summary field exists but lacks the specific entity names, descriptions, or search terms needed for effective retrieval in the next hop.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When solver produces no summary at all (use A code for missing output). When retrieval fails due to external system issues rather than summary quality. When the summary is clear but retrieval system itself malfunctions.
detection_heuristics: Summary uses pronouns or vague references instead of explicit entity names
Summary says 'need more information' without specifying what entities to search for
Summary contains ambiguous descriptions that could match multiple entities
Summary omits key identifying details (dates, full names, locations) needed for precise retrieval
Next retrieval hop returns irrelevant results due to insufficient query specificity
Multiple entities mentioned in claim but summary only names some of them

category_b.name: Solver_Incorrect_Entity_Resolution
category_b.definition: Solver incorrectly identifies which entity a claim is referring to, leading to retrieval and verification of the wrong entity. The solver confuses similar names, assigns attributes to the wrong person/organization, or misinterprets referents in the claim.
category_b.when_to_use: When solver explicitly identifies an entity by name but selects the wrong one (e.g., wrong person with same name, wrong organization with similar name).
category_b.when_not_to_use: When solver simply fails to name any entity (use B.1). When the claim itself is ambiguous about which entity is meant (use coordinator codes). When solver correctly identifies entity but extracts wrong facts about it (use B.3).
detection_heuristics: Solver retrieves information about 'John Smith the actor' when claim refers to 'John Smith the politician'
Solver verifies facts about the wrong organization with a similar name
Solver assigns attributes from one entity to another entity mentioned in same passages
Solver confuses parent/subsidiary organizations or related entities

category_b.name: Solver_Incorrect_Fact_Extraction
category_b.definition: Solver extracts incorrect factual information from passages, misreading dates, numbers, relationships, or attributes. The relevant information exists in the passage but solver misinterprets, misreads, or misrepresents it.
category_b.when_to_use: When solver cites passages but gets basic facts wrong (wrong year, wrong number, wrong relationship type, wrong attribute value).
category_b.when_not_to_use: When solver makes logical errors with correctly extracted facts (use B.5). When solver ignores relevant content (use B.6). When passages don't contain the information at all.
detection_heuristics: Solver states 'founded in 1995' when passage says 'founded in 1985'
Solver reports wrong numerical values (revenue, population, measurements)
Solver misreads relationships ('parent company' vs 'subsidiary', 'predecessor' vs 'successor')
Solver confuses similar but distinct attributes (birth date vs death date, start date vs end date)

category_b.name: Solver_Failed_To_Identify_Missing_Evidence
category_b.definition: Solver incorrectly concludes that provided passages are sufficient to verify the claim when critical evidence is missing. Solver reaches a definitive verdict (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) without having the necessary information to do so.
category_b.when_to_use: When solver makes final judgment but passages lack key information needed to verify the claim. Solver should have recognized information gap and requested more retrieval.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When solver correctly identifies missing evidence and requests more retrieval. When all necessary evidence is present but solver fails to use it (use B.6). When workflow is prematurely terminated by coordinator (use B.11).
detection_heuristics: Solver concludes SUPPORTS/REFUTES but passages don't contain information about key claim components
Claim requires verification of multiple facts but solver only verified some
Solver makes assumptions to fill information gaps rather than acknowledging gaps
Solver verdict contradicts their own statement that 'passages don't mention X' where X is critical to the claim

category_b.name: Solver_Incorrect_Logical_Inference
category_b.definition: Solver draws incorrect logical conclusions from correctly extracted facts. The solver accurately reads passage content but makes reasoning errors in how facts combine, what they imply, or how they relate to the claim.
category_b.when_to_use: When solver extracts facts correctly but reasoning from facts to conclusion is flawed (invalid logical steps, incorrect comparison, wrong temporal reasoning, faulty causation).
category_b.when_not_to_use: When solver misreads the facts themselves (use B.3). When solver ignores available facts (use B.6). When the logical strategy is wrong for multi-hop claims (use B.7).
detection_heuristics: Solver correctly notes 'A happened in 1990' and 'B happened in 1995' but concludes 'B happened before A'
Solver extracts two facts correctly but makes invalid inference about their relationship
Solver applies incorrect logical operator (treats 'and' as 'or', treats 'all' as 'some')
Solver makes temporal reasoning error with correctly extracted dates
Solver confuses correlation with causation in reasoning

category_b.name: Solver_Ignored_Relevant_Passage_Content
category_b.definition: Solver fails to incorporate relevant information from provided passages into its analysis. Passages contain information directly relevant to the claim but solver overlooks it, doesn't mention it, or doesn't integrate it into reasoning.
category_b.when_to_use: When passages contain information that would change the verdict or strengthen the analysis, but solver doesn't acknowledge or use this information.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When passages don't contain relevant information. When solver extracts information but interprets it incorrectly (use B.3 or B.5). When solver requests information that's already present (may overlap with this code).
detection_heuristics: Passage explicitly states fact relevant to claim but solver's analysis doesn't mention it
Solver says 'passages don't mention X' when they actually do mention X
Solver's summary omits key facts that appear in the passages provided
Solver reaches conclusion without referencing relevant evidence present in passages
Solver focuses on one passage while ignoring other relevant passages provided

category_b.name: Solver_Incorrect_Multi_Hop_Strategy
category_b.definition: Solver uses inappropriate retrieval strategy for multi-hop claims, such as attempting to verify all components simultaneously when sequential resolution is needed, or failing to recognize that intermediate entity resolution is required before final verification.
category_b.when_to_use: When claim requires multi-step verification (identify entity A, then use A to find B, then verify fact about B) but solver doesn't follow appropriate sequential strategy.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When claim is single-hop. When solver uses correct strategy but executes it poorly (use other codes for execution failures). When coordinator's instructions prevent correct strategy (use coordinator codes).
detection_heuristics: Claim requires 'find X's Y, then verify Z about Y' but solver tries to verify Z without first identifying Y
Solver requests all information at once when sequential resolution is needed
Solver doesn't recognize that intermediate step is needed to resolve entity before final fact check
Solver's retrieval plan doesn't reflect dependency structure of multi-hop claim

category_b.name: Coordinator_Incomplete_Task_Specification
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides incomplete or unclear instructions that don't fully specify the verification task requirements or essential workflow context. This includes missing information about verification task requirements, workflow structure, iteration count, termination conditions, or expected output format.
category_b.when_to_use: When coordinator's instructions leave solver without clear understanding of what to do, how many hops are expected, when to terminate, or what constitutes successful completion.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When instructions are clear but solver doesn't follow them (use solver codes). When the claim itself is problematic (use B.9). When initial passages are wrong (use B.10).
detection_heuristics: Instructions don't specify number of retrieval hops expected
Instructions don't clarify termination conditions
Instructions missing information about expected output format or structure
Instructions don't explain workflow stages or solver's role within iteration structure
Instructions contain undefined terms or references without explanation
Solver appears confused about task scope or workflow structure due to instruction gaps

category_b.name: Coordinator_Defective_Claim_Formulation
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides a claim that is structurally defective, ambiguous, or unclear, making verification difficult or impossible. This includes grammatical errors, missing context, ambiguous wording, unclear referents, or structural complexity that obscures what needs verification.
category_b.when_to_use: When the claim text itself has quality problems that impede verification—unclear what entities are referenced, ambiguous what fact is being claimed, or structural issues that make parsing difficult.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When claim is clear but instructions are poor (use B.8). When claim is clear but solver misunderstands it anyway (use solver codes). When claim is inherently complex but well-formed.
detection_heuristics: Claim uses pronouns without clear antecedents
Claim has grammatical errors that create ambiguity about meaning
Claim refers to entities without sufficient identification (which 'John Smith'?)
Claim structure makes it unclear what fact is being asserted
Multiple reasonable interpretations of what claim is asserting
Critical context needed to interpret claim is missing

category_b.name: Coordinator_Inappropriate_Initial_Passages
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides initial passages that are irrelevant, off-topic, or insufficient for beginning the verification process. The starting evidence doesn't relate to the claim or doesn't provide foundation for first verification step.
category_b.when_to_use: When initial passages provided with the claim don't contain information relevant to starting verification. Passages are about wrong topic, wrong entity, or completely unrelated content.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When initial passages are relevant but insufficient (this is expected—solver should request more). When passages are relevant but solver doesn't use them (use B.6). When later retrieval hops return bad passages (that's external system issue).
detection_heuristics: Initial passages are about completely different topic than claim
Initial passages mention different entities than those in claim
Passages provide no starting point for verification process
Solver must immediately request new retrieval because initial passages are unusable

category_b.name: Coordinator_Premature_Task_Termination
category_b.definition: Coordinator terminates the verification workflow before sufficient evidence has been gathered or before the required number of retrieval hops are completed. Workflow ends while solver is still requesting more information or before solver has reached confident verdict.
category_b.when_to_use: When coordinator stops the workflow but solver's last output indicated more retrieval was needed, or when workflow ends before completing expected number of hops without good reason.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When solver indicates verification is complete and coordinator appropriately terminates. When termination happens due to system failure (use A codes). When solver fails to recognize missing evidence (use B.4).
detection_heuristics: Solver's last summary requests more information but no additional hop is provided
Workflow configured for N hops but terminates after fewer hops without clear reason
Solver hasn't reached definitive verdict but workflow ends
Solver explicitly states uncertainty and needs more evidence but workflow terminates

category_b.name: Coordinator_Inconsistent_Task_Instructions
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides task instructions that conflict with each other or with the system architecture. Examples include requesting three hops but evaluation structure only supports two, conflicting success criteria, or instructions that contradict workflow capabilities.
category_b.when_to_use: When instructions contain internal contradictions or mismatches between instructions and actual workflow structure/capabilities.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When instructions are simply incomplete (use B.8). When instructions are clear but solver doesn't follow them (use solver codes).
detection_heuristics: Instructions specify N retrieval hops but system architecture supports different number
Instructions describe workflow that doesn't match actual execution structure
Conflicting success criteria provided in different parts of instructions
Instructions request capabilities that system doesn't have
Evaluation criteria inconsistent with task instructions

category_b.name: Solver_Degrading_Output_Quality
category_b.definition: Solver's output quality progressively deteriorates across retrieval hops—reasoning becomes less coherent, analysis becomes more superficial, responses become shorter or more generic, or solver appears to lose track of the verification goal in later iterations.
category_b.when_to_use: When comparing solver outputs across hops within same task shows clear quality decline. Early hops have detailed reasoning but later hops are superficial or confused.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When quality is consistently poor across all hops (use other specific codes for the quality issues). When later hops are shorter because task is nearly complete. When system produces truncated output (use A codes).
detection_heuristics: First hop has detailed analysis, later hops have minimal analysis
Reasoning coherence decreases in later hops
Solver seems to forget earlier findings in later hops
Later summaries are less specific than earlier ones
Signs of repetition or confusion increase in later iterations
Solver restarts analysis in later hops rather than building on earlier work

category_b.name: Solver_Instruction_Drift
category_b.definition: Solver deviates from its specified task instructions, answering a different question than asked, following wrong workflow steps, ignoring explicit constraints, or changing its interpretation of the task mid-workflow.
category_b.when_to_use: When solver's behavior clearly violates explicit instructions provided by coordinator. Solver does something it was told not to do or doesn't do something it was told to do.
category_b.when_not_to_use: When instructions were unclear (use B.8). When solver follows instructions but performs poorly (use other quality codes). When solver makes reasoning errors while trying to follow instructions (use B.5).
detection_heuristics: Instructions say 'verify X' but solver verifies Y instead
Instructions specify output format but solver uses different format
Instructions say 'do not make assumptions' but solver makes assumptions
Solver's approach contradicts explicit methodological guidance in instructions
Solver answers different question than posed in claim
Solver ignores explicit constraints on what evidence to consider

category_c.name: Incomplete_Claim_Verification
category_c.definition: Concluding that a claim is verified or refuted without obtaining or analyzing all necessary evidence components required by the claim structure, including conjunctive requirements (multiple conditions connected by 'and'), comparative requirements (both sides of a comparison), or conditional requirements (both antecedent and consequent).
category_c.when_to_use: When the trace shows a definitive verification conclusion (supported/refuted) but evidence for one or more required claim components is missing or not analyzed. This includes: (1) conjunctive claims where only subset of conditions verified, (2) comparative claims where only one entity verified, (3) conditional claims where only consequent verified without antecedent, (4) claims with multiple attributes where only some checked.
category_c.when_not_to_use: Do not use when all claim components were checked but the analysis was incorrect (use other C codes for analysis errors). Do not use when the conclusion explicitly states uncertainty or insufficient evidence (not a verification conclusion). Do not use for retrieval failures alone without a premature conclusion.
detection_heuristics: Claim contains 'and' or 'both' but trace only verifies one component
Claim requires comparison ('more than', 'before', 'higher') but only one entity is analyzed
Claim is conditional ('if X then Y') but only Y is verified
Claim has multiple factual requirements but trace skips checking some
Definitive conclusion ('supported', 'refuted') appears before all claim components addressed
Trace says 'verified' but claim structure indicates multiple requirements not all checked

category_c.name: Entity_Misidentification
category_c.definition: Incorrectly matching, conflating, or distinguishing entities (people, places, works, organizations) that have similar names, overlapping attributes, or ambiguous references.
category_c.when_to_use: When reasoning treats two distinct entities as the same, or treats one entity as multiple entities, based on name similarity or shared attributes without proper disambiguation.
category_c.when_not_to_use: When entity identification is correct, or when reasoning explicitly acknowledges ambiguity and requests clarification.
detection_heuristics: Reasoning matches entities based solely on first name (e.g., 'Olivia' matching any Olivia)
Conflating different works with similar titles
Assuming entity identity without checking distinguishing attributes (nationality, dates, roles)
Passages mention multiple candidates but reasoning doesn't differentiate

category_c.name: Missing_Relationship_Evidence
category_c.definition: Having evidence for individual claim components (entity A's properties, entity B's properties) but lacking the specific relational evidence that connects them, or failing to properly chain evidence across multiple hops to establish transitive relationships required by the claim.
category_c.when_to_use: When the trace establishes facts about individual entities but the claim requires a relationship between them that is not evidenced. This includes: (1) knowing A's attributes and B's attributes but not whether A relates to B, (2) having A→B and B→C but failing to chain them to establish A→C, (3) having indirect evidence but missing the direct connection needed, (4) having temporal or spatial co-occurrence without causal or direct relationship evidence.
category_c.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the relationship evidence exists but is misinterpreted (use C.13). Do not use when one entity's properties are missing entirely (use C.1). Do not use when the inference about relationship is unsupported but passages are sufficient (use C.8).
detection_heuristics: Claim requires 'X worked with Y' but passages only show X's career and Y's career separately
Claim requires 'X created Y' but passages show X's works and Y's existence without connection
Multi-hop claim (A→B→C) where passages provide A→B and B→C but trace doesn't chain them
Claim requires causal or direct relationship but passages only show correlation or co-occurrence
Trace concludes relationship exists based on entity proximity in passages without explicit relationship statement

category_c.name: Attribute_Contradiction_Ignored
category_c.definition: Failing to recognize or flag when passage evidence directly contradicts a specific attribute value stated in the claim (nationality, date, location, role, quantity, etc.), either by overlooking the contradiction or by incorrectly rationalizing contradictory values as compatible.
category_c.when_to_use: When passages contain explicit information that contradicts a claim attribute, but the trace either: (1) doesn't notice the contradiction, (2) notices but dismisses it without valid justification, (3) treats contradictory values as compatible through invalid reasoning, (4) selectively uses only the supporting evidence while ignoring contradicting evidence.
category_c.when_not_to_use: Do not use when passages don't contain contradicting information (use C.7 for missing information). Do not use when ambiguous phrasing leads to apparent contradiction (use C.18). Do not use when different sources legitimately disagree (use C.19 for source conflation issues).
detection_heuristics: Claim states date X, passage states different date Y, trace doesn't flag mismatch
Claim states nationality/location X, passage states Y, trace concludes 'supported'
Claim states quantity/count X, passage states Y, trace doesn't identify contradiction
Passage explicitly states 'not X' or 'contrary to X' but trace treats as supporting X
Trace acknowledges difference but incorrectly rationalizes as compatible (e.g., 'both could be true')

category_c.name: Unsupported_Inference_From_Passages
category_c.definition: Making logical inferences that go beyond what passages explicitly state, based on partial matches, implicit assumptions, domain knowledge not present in the evidence, or treating related/tangential information as if it directly supports the claim.
category_c.when_to_use: When the trace concludes something that requires assumptions or reasoning not grounded in passage text. This includes: (1) inferring specific facts from general statements, (2) assuming properties based on category membership without evidence, (3) treating passages about related topics as evidence for specific claim, (4) making causal inferences from correlations, (5) using implicit assumptions without acknowledging them.
category_c.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the inference is explicitly stated in passages (use C.13 if misquoted). Do not use when the issue is missing evidence rather than inference (use C.7). Do not use for entity confusion (use C.2).
detection_heuristics: Trace concludes specific fact but passages only provide general category information
Trace uses passage about related entity/topic to verify claim about different entity
Trace makes assumption based on typical patterns ('usually', 'typically') not stated in passages
Passage states A, trace concludes B where A→B requires unstated assumption
Trace treats tangential mention or context as direct evidence
Reasoning includes phrases like 'likely', 'probably', 'would imply' without passage support

category_c.name: Insufficient_Evidence_Not_Flagged
category_c.definition: Failing to identify and explicitly flag when retrieved passages are insufficient for verification because they lack critical information, even when the system should recognize the gap.
category_c.when_to_use: When passages clearly don't contain necessary evidence for claim components, but reasoning proceeds without requesting additional retrieval or flagging the insufficiency.
category_c.when_not_to_use: When insufficient evidence is correctly identified in the summary, or when passages actually do contain sufficient evidence.
detection_heuristics: Summary gives definitive answer but passages don't fully support it
No passage addresses specific claim component but this isn't mentioned
Reasoning skips over claim components without evidence
No explicit statement like 'missing evidence for X' when evidence is absent

category_c.name: Quantifier_Scope_Error
category_c.definition: Misinterpreting or ignoring the scope of quantifiers and modifiers in claims (all/some/exactly, only/also, first/last, most/least, etc.), leading to verification of a different claim than stated.
category_c.when_to_use: When claim contains specific quantifiers or restrictive modifiers but reasoning treats the claim as if it had broader or narrower scope.
category_c.when_not_to_use: When quantifiers are correctly interpreted and applied in the verification process.
detection_heuristics: Claim says 'the film' (definite) but reasoning verifies 'a film' (indefinite)
Claim includes 'also worked as' (conjunction) but reasoning only checks one role
Claim specifies 'exactly three' or 'only' but reasoning ignores the restriction
Temporal modifiers like 'before', 'after', 'during' not properly verified

category_c.name: Numerical_Calculation_Error
category_c.definition: Errors in calculating or comparing numerical values required by the claim, including dates, counts, durations, or rankings.
category_c.when_to_use: When claim requires numerical computation (date differences, enrollment comparisons, counting) but the reasoning contains arithmetic errors or incorrect comparisons.
category_c.when_not_to_use: When numerical reasoning is correct, or when passages don't provide the numerical information needed.
detection_heuristics: Claim asks if X years before/after but calculation is wrong (e.g., 2016 - 12 = 2004)
Comparing enrollment numbers but getting comparison direction wrong
Counting entities incorrectly from passages
Date arithmetic errors visible in reasoning

category_c.name: Reference_Resolution_Failure
category_c.definition: Failing to correctly resolve pronouns, definite descriptions, or anaphoric references in the claim to identify what entities or concepts they refer to.
category_c.when_to_use: When claim contains references like 'the film he acted in', 'the institution where X received degree', 'the same nightclub' but reasoning doesn't correctly identify the referent.
category_c.when_not_to_use: When all references are correctly resolved to their antecedents.
detection_heuristics: Claim says 'the film Alec Utgoff acted in' but reasoning doesn't identify which film
References like 'the same X' or 'that Y' treated incorrectly
Possessive references ('his film', 'their work') not properly resolved
Reasoning retrieves information for wrong referent

category_c.name: Passage_Misrepresentation
category_c.definition: Misquoting, paraphrasing incorrectly, or misrepresenting what passages actually state, including selective quotation that changes meaning, misreading text, or inverting the sense of statements (treating negative as positive or vice versa).
category_c.when_to_use: When comparing the trace's characterization of passage content to the actual passage text reveals: (1) direct misquotation, (2) paraphrase that changes meaning, (3) selective quotation removing critical qualifiers, (4) stating passage says X when it says opposite or different thing, (5) adding information not present in passage.
category_c.when_not_to_use: Do not use when passage is correctly quoted but incorrectly interpreted for verification (use C.5 for unsupported inference). Do not use when passage is irrelevant but correctly quoted (use C.5). Do not use for entity confusion (use C.2).
detection_heuristics: Trace quotes passage with words that don't appear in actual passage text
Trace says 'passage states X' but passage actually states not-X or opposite
Passage includes qualifier ('may', 'possibly', 'according to some') but trace drops it
Trace combines information from multiple sentences as if single statement
Passage uses conditional or hypothetical but trace treats as factual statement
Trace reverses subject and object of passage statement

category_c.name: Retrieval_Strategy_Incoherence
category_c.definition: Requesting or performing retrievals that are illogical given the current evidence state, such as retrieving redundant information or failing to retrieve the next logical link in a chain.
category_c.when_to_use: When the sequence or content of retrievals doesn't follow a coherent strategy for gathering the evidence needed to verify the claim components.
category_c.when_not_to_use: When retrieval strategy is appropriate for the multi-hop verification task, even if passages retrieved turn out to be insufficient.
detection_heuristics: Retrieving same entity multiple times without new angle
Having evidence for A→B but retrieving more about A instead of looking for B→C
Retrieval requests don't target missing claim components
Random-appearing retrieval sequence with no logical progression

category_c.name: Ambiguous_Phrasing_Misinterpreted

category_c.name: Temporal_Reasoning_Error
